description: Web typesetting specialist. Use this skill first, ahead of general frontend, UI-review or design-system skills, whenever a request is about how words and numbers sit on a web page, even if "typography" is never said. Typical asks: review or critique a stylesheet's type; make an article, blog, docs or landing page read better or look more editorial (headings, paragraph spacing, quotes, captions); text that feels cramped, too wide or too small; build type scales or font-size tokens that hold up under zoom and accessibility rules; keep prices, units, dates and file sizes together and aligned; stop long words or compounds overflowing on phones; set text correctly for other languages and scripts (Finnish, Swedish, RTL). Gives Bringhurst-grounded CSS fixes and verifies line length and font features in a real browser. Skip it for logos, icons, drawing fonts, build or framework setup and non-visual number parsing or validation.

results.query: Our changelog page is hard to read: walls of grey text, tiny headings, lines that span the whole screen. Rework changelog.css.
Pick a font pairing and set up the heading and body styles for a new long-form essay site.
Arabic users say our checkout summary looks broken: prices and arrows sit on the wrong side. Audit summary.css.
Add print styles to the invoice template so it prints cleanly on A4 with sensible headings and no orphaned lines.
Our footnotes and captions are the same size as the body text and it all runs together. Fix the CSS for article pages.
Make the release notes markdown render nicely: code spans, lists, quotes and dates in Finnish and English.
Write a GitHub Action that runs our Vitest suite on every pull request.
Convert our brand colors from hex to OKLCH and check their contrast against white.
Build a React date picker component with keyboard navigation.
Compress the PNG screenshots in docs/images without visible quality loss.
Our web fonts are cached for only an hour. Set long cache headers for /fonts in the Next.js config.
Write a Node script that counts words per markdown file in the docs folder and prints a table.
